victim.name: Daniel Cross
victim.note: Found drowned beside a stabbed, partially submerged car. Suicide and homicide interpretations compete. Note: shares a name with a suspect in Case 014 ('The Man Who Moved') — a different, unrelated character in this case's fiction.

suspects.name: Unidentified Second Occupant
suspects.note: Represented by the second blood type and the partial fingerprint recovered from the vehicle; identity not established.

suspects.name: Case-Related Contact (Unidentified)
suspects.relationship_to_victim: possible connection through one of Daniel's prosecutions
suspects.note: Represents the hypothesis that Daniel's professional work as a prosecutor created a motive for someone else.

timeline.event: Daniel is last seen leaving his office
Toll-ticket records place his vehicle on a specific route
The vehicle's final recorded movement occurs before it enters the water
Daniel is found drowned beside the partially submerged, stabbed vehicle

evidence.name: Toll-Ticket Timeline Record
evidence.description: Independent chronology testing Daniel's movements on his last drive.

evidence.name: Rear-Seat Blood Sample (Daniel's)
evidence.description: Blood matching Daniel found in the rear seat, suggesting an event occurred inside the vehicle.

evidence.name: Second Blood-Type Sample
evidence.description: A second blood type recovered from the vehicle, introducing another contributor to the scene.

evidence.name: Partial Fingerprint
evidence.description: An incomplete print providing a possible second-person connection, though not conclusive on its own.

evidence.name: Vehicle Submersion/Damage Report
evidence.description: Documents the condition of the partially submerged vehicle and stab damage.

evidence.name: Scene Position/Stab-Pattern Analysis
evidence.description: Reconstructs the vehicle's final movement and the positioning consistent with the stab damage.

evidence.name: Suicide-vs-Homicide Comparative Report
evidence.description: Compares the competing suicide and homicide explanations against the full physical and timeline record.

puzzles.name: Drive Timeline
puzzles.description: Reconstruct Daniel's movements on his final drive using independent records.

puzzles.name: Blood Pattern
puzzles.description: Interpret the two blood sources recovered from the vehicle.

puzzles.name: Partial Print
puzzles.description: Assess what the incomplete fingerprint can and cannot establish.

puzzles.name: Vehicle Reconstruction
puzzles.description: Reconstruct the vehicle's final movement and damage pattern.

puzzles.name: Suicide vs Homicide Audit
puzzles.description: Compare the competing explanations directly and submit a reconstruction that explicitly separates established facts, plausible inferences, and unresolved questions.
puzzles.ai_initial_behavior: Acts as a devil's advocate, challenging a player who becomes committed too early to either explanation, pushing a strong player toward chronology and physical reconstruction rather than motive-only reasoning.

hypotheses.statement: Daniel was killed by an unidentified second person present in the vehicle.
The physical evidence is ambiguous enough that neither suicide nor homicide can be conclusively established from what is currently known.
